description: Capability for the main DayRail window. Tauri 2's permission system is allowlist-based; nothing the frontend invokes works unless it's permitted here. Keep this minimal — every entry expands the surface that a compromised webview could touch. fs scope strategy: the static allowlist covers only $APPDATA (Y.Doc persistence in ydoc/ + ydoc-dev/, see packages/db/src/tauriFsYDocStore.ts). Every read/write outside app data goes through tauri-plugin-dialog, which adds the user-picked path to the fs runtime scope on its own (allow_file/allow_directory in the dialog plugin) — so .dryj import/export and 下载 flows need no static grant here. Backup files (including a user-configured backup directory) are handled entirely by Rust commands in backup.rs and never touch the webview fs scope.
